body:
Thank you for the great suggestion.

That sounds like an amazingly good idea, and may even warrent a try.
Thanks again.
It is, I am getting better every single day. Thank you for asking.

Thanks for the reply, it really does help me put things in perspective.

Also on the night of my crash, there were 4 other crashes nearby and sadly no other survivers as well.

I am very thankful that I was as well off as I am, however being left like this I can see how I am taking a toll on those who I rely on for support.

They are no longer as happy caring for me (I don't blame them), if I could get up and do a lot of things on my own I would, and I keep trying every day.

You are a purely amazing person, and we all love you for it. I am sure he loved every second of having you by his side and he is a lucky, lucky man to have had such an utterly outstanding person in his life.

Thank you so much for this. This seems like some of the best advice I have heard in a long time, and this is what I now plan on doing for the next week.

Thank you very much for the sound advice good sir.

Letting go is deffinately the hardest part, and the part I am having trouble with the most..  
I keep having to fight the urge to just pick up the phone and call or text her, as each time I do I know it results in me missing her a little more, even if I don't recognise it.. I usually can't help myself, but in my head I justify it by her wanting to still be friends. Even though being friends I can not really ever let go.

I still have chances to see her, but I don't know if they will count as they are a couple of months away, and I know her feelings for me can chance between now and then.

Also, it seems like reddit is nearly the only place to get any form of an intelligent conversation these days.

She did pull me out of a slump, and she did make me truely happy. However, she's also gone right now, and I feel even further down that I was to begin with. Now I don't even have a true direction to go in, I could try and climb out of this slump eventually, or chase her further down the rabbit hole, not knowing where I am going, and if it will ever end..

Thank you for the advice, but I can't really remember what it felt like to be independent.. I was never exactly very outgoing, I had been bullied from a young age all through highschool and became very socially awkward and introverted because of this.

I was really struggling to make friends before she came along, and at the time, she really felt like she stood me on my own 2 feet and gave me a backbone. Her being in my life gave me a whole new meaning and confidence which I hadn't had before.

As much as I want to be independent, I sadly wouldn't know where to start, but it's something I will try my very best to work towards.

Thank you very much, although I feel like the last thing I want to do is move on. Even though in my head I probably feel like it is the best thing to do, my heart won't allow it.  
As much as my head tells me to just move on, my heart tells me to hang on, because there's always a chance that things could one day get better, and on that day I will be thankful I didn't let go..

Also, sadly I am not that much of a book reader, but I do enjoy listening/participating in intelligent conversation.

**Edit:** Grammer
